newsitem.title: LATVIA: Foreigners dominate new Latvia 2-yr T-bill sale.
newsitem.headline: Foreigners dominate new Latvia 2-yr T-bill sale.

text.p: Latvia on Wednesday for the first time sold domestic Treasury bills with a maturity of two years and local banks said that foreign players dominated the auction.
The paper was sold with an average yield of 9.52 percent and all of the 17 million lat issue was sold as investors entered bids worth 48.32 million lats.
"Mainly big foreign investors participated in the two-year paper auction," Maris Vinklers, the head of money markets at Hansabank-Latvija, told Reuters.

"Demand for the two-year T-bills may be subdued on the local market as Latvian banks perhaps are not so sure about their financial stability in the long term," a foreign exchange dealer in a leading commercial bank said.
The launch of the two-year paper is part of the finance ministry's efforts to lengthen Latvia's debt maturity and get away from too much short-term, one month paper.

Short-term paper has traditionally been popular in the volatile world of Latvian banking and finance as investors have been reluctant to place their money for longer due to fears of political and financial instability.
But trust has been gradually growing and the finance ministry next year plans to launch five-year T-bills.
Most players did not expect an immediate effect on the inter-bank market following the launch of two-year paper.
"I would not see any immediate effects on the over-night market except for a possibility of an inter-bank deposit market developing," a dealer said.
"We now have a longer-term benchmark," he added.
